newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to provide soft loans to Korea First Bank.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to provide soft loans to Korea First Bank.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry and the central bank have agreed to offer soft loans to Korea First Bank, which is suffering from bad loans, local newspapers reported on Sunday.
The soft loans will be provided from a state fund being set up under a bill passed through parliament last month, dailies Joongang Ilbo and Kyunghyang Shinmun said.

The fund is aimed at reducing non-performing loans of the country's commercial banks which had to offer loans at artificially low rates to finance "key industrial projects" designated by the government in the 1970s and the 1980s.

The newspapers said the decision on the soft loans was made in a meeting on Saturday between Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik, central bank governor Lee Kyung-shick and Kim In-ho, chief economic advisor to President Kim young-sam.
The newspaper reports gave no details on the size and terms of soft loans but said the state fund would take over Korea First Bank's bad loans and collateral.
Korea First Bank has been hit by a string of debt payment defaults by some of its major clients, including the Hanbo Group and the Kia Group.

The Hanbo Group's flagship, Hanbo Steel Co, the country's second largest steelmaker was declared insolvent in January, while the Gia Group has been put under two months protection by banks from defaulting on debt payments.
Joongang Ilbo said the central bank, the Bank of Korea, would also consider extending special loans to Korea First Bank only after reviewing the commercial bank's self-rescue plans.
Korea First Bank had already asked for three trillion won in special loans from the central bank.
